cases.name: trust proxy: true · Request: Client via the CDN

steps.title: Two ways into one app
steps.line: The load balancer also accepts connections from the internet.
steps.caption: Requests are meant to reach Express through a CDN and then a load balancer, but the load balancer also accepts connections from the internet, so an attacker can skip the CDN. The addresses are examples. Assumed throughout: each proxy appends the address its connection came from to X-Forwarded-For.
steps.picture: Architecture diagram: 5 services, 5 edges; “Addresses”, 4 labelled values; “This case”, 2 labelled values; 2 labels.

steps.title: The client’s request gains one address at each proxy
steps.line: Each of two proxies appends one: two entries reach Express.
steps.caption: The client sends no X-Forwarded-For. The CDN edge appends the client’s address, 203.0.113.7, and the load balancer appends the edge’s, 192.0.2.10. Express receives that header on a connection from the load balancer, so its socket address is 10.0.0.5.

steps.title: trust proxy true trusts every address
steps.line: Every address passes the check, so the loop never stops early.
steps.caption: Express turns the setting into a trust function. true trusts every address. proxy-addr lists the socket address, then X-Forwarded-For from right to left, and stops at the first address it does not trust. req.ip is the last address in its list.

steps.title: req.ip is 203.0.113.7, the client’s real address
steps.line: Express trusts two addresses and reaches the end of the list.
steps.caption: true trusts every address, so Express reads to the end of the list. The list ends at 203.0.113.7, so that is req.ip. That is the client’s real address.
